# Existing Data Model

The current ORM defines 13 SQLAlchemy tables in `backend/models.py`. All IDs are integer primary keys; relationships use foreign keys and ORM cascades as described.

| Entity / table | Fields | Relationships |
|---|---|---|
| `Song` / `songs` | `id`, `title`, `artist`, `genre`, `lyrics`, `bpm`, `musical_key`, `energy`, `valence`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at` | Has many runs, campaigns, and release-calendar entries. |
| `CampaignPlan` / `campaign_plans` | `id`, `song_id`, `name`, `objective`, `status`, `release_date`, `budget_total`, `channels`, `notes`, `created_at` | Belongs to song; has many tasks and calendar entries. |
| `CampaignTask` / `campaign_tasks` | `id`, `campaign_id`, `name`, `channel`, `owner`, `priority`, `due_in_days`, `status`, `description`, `created_at` | Belongs to campaign. |
| `ArtistProfile` / `artist_profiles` | `id`, `name`, `brand_voice`, `target_audience`, `goals`, `markets`, `created_at` | Standalone profile; endpoints select the most recently created row. |
| `ReleaseCalendarEntry` / `release_calendar_entries` | `id`, `song_id`, `campaign_id`, `title`, `entry_type`, `channel`, `scheduled_for`, `status`, `notes`, `created_at` | Optionally belongs to song and campaign; both foreign keys use `SET NULL`. |
| `Run` / `runs` | `id`, `song_id`, `status`, `error`, `logs`, `started_at`, `finished_at` | Belongs to song; one intelligence, one strategy, one metrics row, one optimization report, one final strategy, and many audience/content rows. |
| `SongIntelligenceRow` / `song_intelligence` | `id`, `run_id`, `bpm`, `musical_key`, `energy`, `valence`, `mood`, `structure`, `hooks`, `lyrical_themes`, `production_notes`, `a_r_insights` | One-to-one with run (`run_id` unique). |
| `AudienceSegmentRow` / `audience_segments` | `id`, `run_id`, `name`, `description`, `age_range`, `interests`, `platform_affinity`, `match_score`, `is_primary`, `rank` | Many-to-one with run. |
| `ContentPieceRow` / `content_pieces` | `id`, `run_id`, `format`, `hook`, `concept`, `caption`, `cta`, `sound_strategy`, `sort_index` | Many-to-one with run. |
| `MarketingStrategyRow` / `marketing_strategies` | `id`, `run_id`, `release_type`, `timeline_weeks`, `phases`, `platform_priority`, `budget_allocation`, `pitch_targets`, `key_message` | One-to-one with run (`run_id` unique). |
| `PerformanceMetricsRow` / `performance_metrics` | `id`, `run_id`, `streams`, `saves`, `playlist_adds`, `social_views`, `engagement_rate`, `follower_delta`, `score` | One-to-one with run (`run_id` unique). Values are simulated by the current analytics agent. |
| `OptimizationReportRow` / `optimization_reports` | `id`, `run_id`, `what_worked`, `what_underperformed`, `recommendations`, `lessons_learned` | One-to-one with run (`run_id` unique). |
| `FinalStrategyRow` / `final_strategies` | `id`, `run_id`, `orchestrator_summary`, `top_priority_actions` | One-to-one with run (`run_id` unique). |

JSON columns store list/dict structures for agent outputs and artist/campaign fields. `Song` owns cascading run/campaign/calendar collections; `Run` owns cascading output rows; `CampaignPlan` owns cascading task rows. The current startup path uses `Base.metadata.create_all`, with no Alembic migration history identified. The SQLite database has not been migrated or modified as part of architecture analysis.

## Delivered v1 domain tables

The versioned private workspace uses separate `v1_*` tables so legacy records and contracts remain unchanged. `v1_artist_profiles` stores one artist context per configured owner (`display_name`, optional bio/genre/language/brand voice, territory and goal lists, onboarding completion time, and timestamps). `v1_songs` stores owner-scoped songs; the dashboard queries these by owner using a stable `(created_at, id)` cursor and returns a total count. Profile context supplies missing artist name, language, and primary genre defaults when a song record is created. `v1_rights_declarations` records separate recording/composition rights bases for each song. `v1_consent_records` records scoped processing, derived-analysis-storage, provider, promotional-asset-generation, and platform-account-connection grants and withdrawal events independently. Upload and verification require active processing consent and a rights declaration; analysis also requires active derived-analysis-storage consent. External AI report generation additionally requires a distinct third-party AI grant, rechecked by the worker. Video rendering additionally requires active promotional-asset-generation consent, rechecked by the worker at progress checkpoints. OAuth connections require workspace-level platform-account consent. `v1_platform_connections` stores one owner/provider account identity, granted read-only scopes, token expiry, and Fernet-encrypted access/refresh tokens; plaintext credentials are never returned through the API. `v1_platform_oauth_states` stores only a SHA-256 hash of a provider/owner-bound state value with a ten-minute expiry and one-time consumed marker. Withdrawing platform consent clears stored credentials and invalidates pending OAuth states; disconnecting clears local credentials, while provider-side grant revocation remains a separate user action. `v1_analysis_lyrics` holds only local derived lyric themes and repeated-line candidates, never the submitted full lyric text. Audience hypotheses are generated on demand from an owner's completed Song Intelligence and artist-selected context; they are not persisted as performance observations. `v1_release_plans` stores an owner-scoped release date, goal, draft/approved state, and relative task calendar. `v1_video_renders` stores the owner/song/verified-asset/job relationship, approved format, queued/running/terminal state, progress, render settings, scene plan, source provenance, validated output metadata, checksum, byte size, and completion time. Its MP4 lives in the private media directory, not in SQLite. Plan approval is internal only and cannot execute external actions. Existing profile/calendar routes remain legacy and are not used as owner-scoped v1 data.

`v1_agent_pipeline_runs` stores one latest deterministic five-agent pipeline result per completed analysis, scoped to the same owner. Re-running replaces the prior JSON result and timestamp. Pipeline execution requires current rights, audio-processing consent, and derived-analysis-storage consent; it uses song metadata, structured tempo/key estimates, and derived lyric candidates, not the original audio or full lyric text. The pipeline's generic audience scores and simulated campaign metrics are explicitly not observations or forecasts.
